title: IT’S A SCAM! DON’T DOWNLOAD IT!!!
body:
This app is a complete scam. Don’t download it under any circumstances. I initially selected the €1 option and started using the app. Then, about a week later — out of nowhere and without any notice or consent — they sneakily charged €38.99 from my card. It’s clearly designed to catch users off guard, hoping they’ll forget about the app and miss the charge.

As soon as I saw it, I blocked my card through my banking app — and thank goodness I did, because right after that, they tried to charge €48.99 more. Even though it was declined and I contacted them by email, their system has continued to automatically attempt that same €48.99 charge every single day.

They said a refund was issued and sent a receipt claiming it would arrive in 10 days. I’m still waiting. When I followed up again, Outlook warned me that their email address no longer exists. Other users have reported even worse: some couldn’t reach them at all and never received any reply.

Honestly, I believe the only reason I got a response was because I threatened legal action — and I meant it. If this isn’t resolved within a few days, I’ll move forward with legal steps.

To make things worse, you can’t remove or even view your card details in the app. And this isn’t an App Store purchase — it’s processed through their own shady system. Even now, their system keeps trying to take money from my card every day. Who knows what other amounts they would’ve attempted to charge if I hadn’t blocked it. At this point, I’ll probably have to speak to my bank about changing my card number entirely just to stop them for good.

Avoid this app at all costs — unless you’re okay with being charged repeatedly, without your consent, and with no way to stop it.

title: From bad to worse and pseudoscientific
body:
I enthusiastically endorsed the Fabulous a few years ago and even recommended it to my friends.

Then the app started freezing. I reach out to the helpdesk, hoping that for the premium price I pay, I will get premium support. It takes months before I get an answer.

More recently, this app - while claiming it uses science to improve our lives - is pushing pseudoscientific nonsense like MBTI, a personality type assessment long debunked. When I reached out to the Fabulous team about this... no reaction.

And now, the app simply crashes. One time you’ll open it, and there will be live challenges, but no routines. Another time, you can find your routines, but when you click on them, the app freezes. The one thing it never does: just function as it should.

By now I feel this app has gotten so far away from its stated intention that it’s just another scammer. They have lost me as a subscriber.

title: You get what you give
body:
As a content user I read the reviews with a growing feeling of annoyance. 

Yes, it all starts with drinking water. That is so easy anyone can do it. It’s a tried and true method to start with the no-brainer and step it up gradually. The sense of accomplishment keeps you going. Trust me: it gets a lot harder after a while.

Yes, subsciption is optional if you want the full Fabulous experience. Do you really feel like it’s fair to expect an ad-free app that has such a big team behind it without paying a dime for it? If you get the service, the least you can do is pay for it. Or do you also get your car filled up and drive away without paying?

The free version is a nice starting point, do read the fine print though so you do not accidentally sign up for the free trial with additional subscription when you don’t want to. That said, the amount of reminders to get the yearly subscription is actually a bit overkill. Once you get the hang of it with the free version and discover the amount of features (it is really a quite elaborate app, navigating it is like a treasure hunt) I’m sure you will want to get a premium for a year and to be honest: at 42,99 a year it’s cheaper than my library subscription and well worth the investment.
